colors.name: --primary-*
colors.reason: A stepped brand scale keeps buttons, links, and focus rings in the same color family.

colors.name: --grayscale-*
colors.reason: A numbered neutral scale makes contrast relationships readable from backgrounds through body text.

colors.name: --color-surface
colors.reason: This semantic name describes the role of cards and panels instead of tying components to a specific color.

colors.name: --color-text-muted
colors.reason: Muted text is separated clearly for supporting descriptions and metadata.

colors.name: --accent-hot / --accent-mint
colors.reason: These supporting colors add emphasis while keeping names tied to role and temperature.

colors.name: --gallery-*
colors.reason: Gallery tokens use their own namespace so editorial gallery styling does not conflict with portfolio tokens.

spacing.name: --space-1 ~ --space-11
spacing.reason: Dense UI spacing inside chips, buttons, and cards follows a numbered 4px-based scale.

spacing.name: --space-fluid-xs ~ 3xl
spacing.reason: Fluid spacing allows more room on desktop while preserving information density on tablet and mobile.

spacing.name: --space-section-y / gap
spacing.reason: Section padding and internal gaps are prioritized through breakpoint-specific CSS variable overrides.

spacing.name: --inset-page / --inset-panel
spacing.reason: Separate page and panel insets prevent cards from becoming too narrow on mobile.

spacing.name: --card-padding / lg
spacing.reason: Repeated card padding stays in a card namespace and reduces to the 16px range on mobile.

spacing.name: --size-touch / compact
spacing.reason: Button and toggle sizes are separated around accessible touch target requirements.

typography.name: Display-1
typography.reason: The highest-level token is reserved for the home hero and strongest activity titles.

typography.name: Display-2 / Display-3
typography.reason: These keep a strong visual signal without competing with Display-1.

typography.name: Display-4 / Display-5 / Display-6
typography.reason: These levels separate section titles, major card titles, and small module headings.

typography.name: Title-1 / Title-2 / Title-3
typography.reason: Information headings inside cards and lists stay below the Display scale.

typography.name: Body-1 / Body-2
typography.reason: Body text starts at 16px, while supporting descriptions use a denser 15px size.

typography.name: Label / Chip
typography.reason: Metadata labels use 14px and chips use a fixed 12px minimum to keep small UI consistent.

shapes.name: --radius-card
shapes.reason: The shared radius for primary cards and buttons sets the portfolio's soft baseline.

shapes.name: --radius-pill
shapes.reason: The name clearly identifies pill UI such as tags, segments, and small states.

shapes.name: --shadow-soft
shapes.reason: The default elevation shadow shows hierarchy without excessive decoration.

shapes.name: --shadow-ring
shapes.reason: The ring name describes feedback that surrounds keyboard focus and selected states.

about.intro: Hi, I am Eunyounghwan. I turn complex requirements into interfaces users can understand and code that teammates can continue to develop and operate.
paragraphs: My work covers requirements, markup architecture, CMS customization, responsive implementation, and maintenance across the full UI lifecycle.

My core is HTML, SCSS, and JavaScript web publishing. I maintain UI quality across ICE CMS, WebSquare, and Nexacro, while Vue 3 projects have expanded my role into components, state, routing, and API integration.

On a TMS operations project, I classified recurring issues and improved the UI, bringing daily inconvenience reports from 15+ to around 2. I now feed repeated delivery problems back into shared components and an in-house Nuxt 3 framework.
